chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab and Ahmad b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Faddal narrated to us from Ali b. Asbat from al-Hasan b. Zayd. He said: Muhammad b. Salim narrated to me from al-Asbagh b. Nubata. He said: The Commander of the Believers (as) said:

Uthman b. Affan asked the Messenger of Allah (s): O Messenger of Allah! What is the interpretation of the alphabet? So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: Learn the interpretation of the alphabet, for therein is all wonders. Woe to a scholar who is ignorant of its interpretation. So, it was said: O Messenger of Allah! What is the interpretation of the alphabet? He said:

As for Alif, it is the signs of Allah, a letter from His names. As for Ba, it is the delight of Allah. As for Jim, it is the Paradise of Allah, the majesty of Allah, and His beauty. As for Dal, it is the religion of Allah. As for Hawwaz, Ha is the Ha of the Abyss, so woe to whoever falls into the Fire. As for Waw, woe to the people of the Fire. As for Zay, it is a corner of Hell, and we seek refuge in Allah from what is in the corner, meaning the corners of Hellfire. As for Hutti, Ha is the dropping of sins from those who repent on the Night of Power, and what descends with Gabriel and the angels until the rise of dawn. As for Ta, Tuba is for them and a goodly reward, and it is a tree that Allah has planted, breathing into it of His spirit, and its branches can be seen from behind the fence of Paradise, sprouting jewels and garments, hanging over their mouths. As for Ya, it is the hand of Allah over His creation, glorified and exalted above what they associate. As for Kalamun, Kaf is the words of Allah, there is no change for the words of Allah, and you will never find besides Him a refuge. As for Lam, it is the familiarity of the people of Paradise among them in visits, greetings, and peace, and the mutual blame of the people of the Fire. As for Mim, it is the dominion of Allah that does not diminish and the permanence of Allah that does not perish. As for Nun, Nun and the Pen and what they inscribe, the Pen is a pen of light and a book of light in a Preserved Tablet, witnessed by those brought near, and Allah is sufficient as a Witness. As for Sa'fas, Sad is a measure for a measure and a piece for a piece, meaning the reward for the reward, and as you sow, so shall you reap, for Allah does not wish injustice for His servants. As for Qarashat, it means He gathers them and resurrects them and distributes them until the Day of Resurrection, so He judges between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad explain about the mystical meaning of the Arabic alphabet?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (as) narrates that Uthman b. Affan asked the Prophet (s) about the interpretation of the Arabic alphabet (abjad). The Prophet instructed the people to learn it, declaring that it contains all wonders and warning against scholars who are ignorant of its meaning. He then gave a detailed explanation of each letter group: Alif represents Allah's signs and names; Ba His delight; Jim His Paradise, majesty, and beauty; Dal His religion. Hawwaz represents the horrors of Hell. Hutti refers to sins being dropped from repentant believers on the Night of Power. Ta references the Tuba tree in Paradise. Ya symbolizes Allah's hand over creation. Kalamun represents the immutability of Allah's words. Lam symbolizes the familiarity of Paradise-dwellers and the mutual blame among Hell-dwellers. Mim represents Allah's eternal dominion. Nun references the Preserved Tablet and the Pen of Light. Sa'fas represents divine reciprocal justice. Qarashat refers to the gathering on the Day of Resurrection where all will be judged fairly.
